cluster_summary: This cluster contains 25 CVEs where user-controlled input is processed without proper validation, leading to code injection, prototype pollution, stack overflow, infinite loops, ReDoS, and resource exhaustion. The vulnerabilities arise from missing bounds checks, missing escaping, insufficient key validation, and unsafe recursion patterns across various libraries.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled binary length fields, size counters, frame lengths, offsets, back-references, or decompressed-size metadata into memory allocation, buffer growth, parsing loops, frame handling, decompression, or resource-consuming work. Report code paths where protocol-specific upper bounds, arithmetic overflow checks, structural consistency checks, or expansion limits are absent before allocation or work expansion. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 4 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should enforce explicit size limits, validate arithmetic and offsets before use, reject malformed or oversized records early, and bound decompression or frame-processing work.

mechanism.missing_guard: protocol-specific upper bounds, arithmetic overflow checks, structural consistency checks, or expansion limits are absent before allocation or work expansion
mechanism.name: unbounded binary length or size field drives resource use
mechanism.sink_shape: memory allocation, buffer growth, parsing loops, frame handling, decompression, or resource-consuming work
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled binary length fields, size counters, frame lengths, offsets, back-references, or decompressed-size metadata
mechanism.typical_fix: enforce explicit size limits, validate arithmetic and offsets before use, reject malformed or oversized records early, and bound decompression or frame-processing work

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Replace recursion with iterative explicit stack or worklist patterns, imposing depth limits.
sub_patterns.name: Missing recursion depth limits in iterative processing
sub_patterns.root_cause: Recursive functions process user-controlled nested data without depth bounds, allowing stack overflow.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Use Array.isArray for type checks and validate length against MAX_ARRAY_LEN; iterate over own keys instead of index range.
sub_patterns.name: Unvalidated array length leading to resource exhaustion
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-controlled length values are used to allocate arrays without maximum bound checks, causing CPU or memory exhaustion.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Coerce indices to numbers, implement separate safe property checks for arrays allowing only numeric indices and 'length'.
sub_patterns.name: Prototype pollution via insufficient array property restriction
sub_patterns.root_cause: Array property access does not restrict to numeric indices and length, allowing access to dangerous properties via prototype chain.
